title: A US charity plans to use AI to monitor its Gaza classrooms for ‘hateful’ speech
source_used: Associated Press via Bozeman Daily Chronicle (AP wire copy)
key_facts: Gaza Children Village, a US charity, plans to record classroom conversations and use AI to flag "hateful" or "inciting" speech.
Founder and CEO Dr David Hasan laid out the plan in a webinar last month; warnings go to him and recordings are stored 72 hours.
It is unclear when monitoring starts, what language will be flagged, or whether teachers, students and families were told.
A board member and a partner aid group raised concerns; the partner said it could reconsider working with the charity.
A Palestinian government spokesperson said classroom surveillance would cross "an important line".
The plan is to deploy it in dozens of classrooms after testing.
quote_evidence: A U.S. charity in Gaza is worried that teachers at its schools might stray from a curriculum it says promotes peace and tolerance, so it plans to record classroom conversations and use artificial intelligence to flag speech deemed “hateful” or “inciting.”
It is unclear when the classroom monitoring is supposed to begin, what specific language will be flagged, and whether teachers, students and their families have been told about the plans.
why_it_matters_hint: AI surveillance of teachers and children in a war zone raises privacy and control questions.
event_date: webinar in Sept 2026; AP report 9 Oct 2026
